description.narrative: The Project will support the establishment of municipal government in Nuku'alofa and will provide high priority urban infrastructure identified in the Nuku'alofa Urban Infrastructure Development Plan (UIDP). The Project will expand upon infrastructure development currently being undertaken in Nuku'alofa through the Nuku'alofa Reconstruction Project (NRP) and the Integrated Urban Development Sector Project (IUDSP).

description.narrative: Access by Nuku?'alofa residents to improved municipal services increased.

Participation of consumers in solid waste collection Nuku'alofa increases by 80% by 2017. Progress/Status: In 2015, 100% of consumers in Nuku'alofa have access to solid waste services. WAL's solid waste collection system is now reaching 90% of households on Tongatapu Island. Data Source: WAL annual reports. Baseline value: 40%

The reliability (24/7 supply) to Nuku'alofa consumers increased to 99.9% by 2017 Progress/Status: The completion of the ICB-TWB01 subproject (Lot 1 Civil works for the rehabilitation and extension of borefields at Mataki'eua and Tongamai and Lot 2 Design and construction of 4,000ms reservoir at Mataki'eua) ensures 100% increase in water storage and elimination of all water leaks in borefield and existing reservoir pipes, valves and fittings, and reliable supply to Nuku'alofa consumers. Data Source: TWB annual reports. Baseline value: Less than 50%
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Raised community awareness of municipal services. Indicator: 50% of individuals trained have reported increased awareness of responsible water and sanitation use (Baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Follow-up surveys with all Nuku'alofa householders indicate that a clear majority (>50%) have an increased understanding and awareness of their obligations to access and pay for improved urban services. Payments for TWB charges continue around 85-90% levels, whilst payment for WAL services have risen from 30-35%, now to >85%. Data Source: TWB and WAL annual reports. Actual value:

Output: Raised community awareness of municipal services. Indicator: By 2015, women represent 50% of participants at general meetings (2011 baseline: limited consultation and/or participation) Progress/Status: Consultations averaged 57% female participation and 43% male. Data Source: TWB and WAL annual reports. Actual value:

Output: Other municipal services within Nuku'alofa improved. Indicator: By Jan 2019: 3 new public conveniences constructed in Nuku'alofa (2016 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Contract for WAL19 construction of two new public convenience buildings at Popua Park and Ma'ufanga Swimming Pool totaling TOP$190,000 awarded to 'Isitolo Lui Construction in May19. Works were completed in May20. Data Source: WAL annual reports Actual value:

Output: Strengthened policy environment for delivery of urban services. Indicator: By Jun 2019, 8 staff with improved skills in sanitation inspection. Progress/Status: 20 people have been formerly designated as sanitation/environmental inspectors (12 Tonga police, 4 environmental staff and 4 public health officials) with project supported skills training and support with sanitation education materials. Data Source: NSPAO quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Other municipal services within Nuku'alofa improved. Indicator: By Jun 2019: 3 new public conveniences constructed at Teufaiva Stadium, Nuku'alfoa (2017 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Contract for WAL30 construction of three new public convenience buildings at Teufavia Stadium totaling TOP$300,000 awarded to Puloka Construction in Feb19. Works were completed in May20. Data Source: WAL annual reports Actual value:

Output: Effective, efficient and sustainable water supply services in Nuku?alofa (core subproject) provided by TWB. Indicator: Losses from the Nuku'alofa water supply network is less than 25% by 2017 (baseline 2011: 50%). Progress/Status: With the completion of the NUDSP-NCB-2014-TWB02 Civil Works for Zoning of Nuku'alofa Water Supply subproject, losses from the network are now assessed to be less than 30%, which is a 40% improvement. Data Source: TWB annual reports. Actual value:

Output: Strengthened policy environment for delivery of urban services. Indicator: TWB (by 2014) and WAL (by 2017) finance 100% of their operation and maintenance costs from sales (2011 baseline: TWB - 95%, WAL - 17%). Progress/Status: TWB now has much improved financing for O&M costs. With improved infrastructure, operational management and a shift to electronically, remotely read water meters system productivity, O&M costs have been reduced. WAL also has much improved financing of O&M costs. WAL has now expanded their waste services and operate a much larger range of vehicles and equipment. Fee increases and improved revenue collections indicate that WAL is now capable of funding 60-70% of their total O&M needs. Data Source: TWB and WAL annual reports. Actual value:

Output: Effective, efficient and sustainable water supply services in Nuku?alofa (core subproject) provided by TWB. Indicator: By Sep 2019: Upgraded IT and office equipment for TWB installed (2016 baseline: not installed) Progress/Status: Upgraded IT and office equipment have been purchased and are being used by TWB. Data Source: TWB annual reports. Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Target year: 2017 Target value: Y

Output: Other municipal services within Nuku'alofa improved. Indicator: At least one priority components of the UIDP is implemented by 2018. (2011 baseline: 0%) Progress/Status: Nuku'alofa Sanitation Masterplan submitted in late 2014 and project proceeded with the supply of a further septage pump truck (supplied 2016) and the construction of 10 new septage drying beds (WAL011) at TWMF. These beds were linked to the existing WWTP and commissioned in Dec19. Data Source: NSPAO annual reports. Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Target year: 2017 Target value: N

Output: Other municipal services within Nuku'alofa improved. Indicator: By Dec 2019: TWMF asset management system updated (2019: baseline: NA) Progress/Status: This work was funded by AF3 which was approved 3Sep19 and was included in PIAC's contract variation of Jan20. Support to WAL was provided through on-the-job training for Tapuhia WMF O&M staff who manage WAL's asset. The support, which was interrupted by COVID-19 pandemic restrictions, was completed in May20. Data Source: WAL annual reports Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Target year: 2017 Target value: N

Output: Other municipal services within Nuku'alofa improved. Indicator: By Dec 2019: upgraded machinery servicing and storage shed installed at Tapuhia Waste Management Facility, Nuku'alofa (2018 baseline: existing shed badly damaged by 2018 cyclone) Progress/Status: This subproject was funded by AF3 which was approved 3Sep19 and in Nov19, contracts (i) for WAL33A Design of Storage Shed totaling $55,000 were awarded to Bluescope Lysaght; and (ii) for WAL33B Construction of Foundation and Erection of Shed totaling TOP279,020 was awarded to Five Star Construction. Due to delays with Cyclone Harold and COVID-19 pandemic, works were completed in May20. Data Source: WAL annual reports Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Target year: 2017 Target value: N

Output: Strengthened policy environment for delivery of urban services. Indicator: National Spatial Planning Authority advisory committee established and comprising at least 40% women by June 2012 (baseline 2011: 0%) Progress/Status: The establishment and composition of the committee is not within the control of the project. Cabinet, Government of Tonga is yet to formally approve the establishment of the National Spatial Planning Authority advisory committee, as well as the nomination and selection process for the formation of this committee. The Minister of Lands continues to act on behalf of the committee. Data Source: NSPAO annual reports and cabinet reports. Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2011 Baseline value: N Target year: 2012 Target value: N

Output: Sustainable solid waste services in Nuku'alofa (core subproject) provided by WAL. Indicator: The Tapuhia Landfill is operated in accordance with the operating procedures specifically developed for the site [DFAT-GOA 2007] by 2015 (baseline 2011: not operated in accordance with the Tapuhia landfill operating procedures) Progress/Status: WAL has significantly improved efforts and funding to follow the DFAT developed Field Operations Manual and QA system but further close attention to service and maintenance quality improvements are required. Retention of trained and experienced operator and driver staff for their specialist vehicles/equipment are an ongoing challenge for WAL. Data Source: WAL annual reports.
